ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text:
For the years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company incurred general and administrative expenses of $47,474 and $47,299 respectively. These were primarily comprised of audit fees, stock and registrar fees, legal fees and other professional fees , and stock-based compensation.

Included in general and administrative expenses were stock-based compensation expenses of $14,000 and $10,000 for the years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively, relating to shares issued to three directors of the Company. As the recipients were directors of the Company, these stock-based compensation expenses were considered related-party transactions.

net.heading: Net Loss
net.text: For the years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company incurred a net loss of $27,474 and $17,299 respectively.

ocf.text: For the year ended July 31, 2026, the Company incurred a net loss of $27,474 and a negative cash flow from operating activities of $14,549. As reflected in the financial statements, the Company had a working capital deficit of $13,104 and an accumulated deficit of $102,669. These conditions raise substantial doubt about the Company’s ability to continue as a going concern. The ability to continue as a going concern is dependent upon the Company’s profit generating operations in the future and/or obtaining the necessary financing to meet its obligations and repay its liabilities arising from normal business operations when they become due. These financial statements do not include any adjustments to the recoverability and classification of recorded asset amounts and classification of liabilities that might be necessary should the Company be unable to continue as a going concern.

sbc.text: Included in general and administrative expenses were stock-based compensation expenses of $14,000 and $10,000 for the years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025, respectively, relating to shares issued to three directors of the Company. As the recipients were directors of the Company, these stock-based compensation expenses were considered related-party transactions.

capex.text: We have no significant off-balance sheet arrangements that have or are reasonably likely to have a current or future effect on our financial condition, changes in our financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures or capital resources that are material to our stockholders as of July 31, 2026.

net sales.heading: Revenues
net sales.text:
For the years ended July 31, 2026 and 2025, the Company has generated a revenue of $20,000 and $30,000 respectively. The revenue is generated through provision of Personal Financial Literacy Seminar (PFL Seminar) services to clients .

During 2025, the Company served one corporate customer and conducted six PFL Seminars for its employees. During 2026, the Company provided PFL Seminar services to four individual customers.

Accordingly, the decrease in revenue from 2025 to 2026 was primarily attributable to the change in customer and participant mix, rather than any material change in the Company’s pricing.
